<!-- An `ar` job answers ONE research question from jobs that have already run.
     It re-runs nothing: each item shows a figure, table or value a finished job
     saved, checked against the bytes that job recorded. The report goes to the
     researchers, who choose which items are published; the publication
     formatting comes after their choice.

     Workflow:
       1. Render the source jobs until each is final.
       2. Name each item below as "<job>#<label>": the job's file name without
          .qmd, and the chunk label it saved under. The job's report shows the
          labels.
       3. From the console: hvtiRtemplates::ar_paste_methods("<this file>").
       4. Write each item's results and interpretation, then render.
       5. When a source job is rendered again, reread the items it feeds and
          run hvtiRtemplates::ar_review("<this file>"). -->

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| results: asis
SUBJECT <- "dead_pa"
TYPE    <- "question"
.in <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(hvtiRutilities))
# The study root is the nearest directory above this file holding _study.yml, so
# the report renders the same from the Render button, quarto render, or
# render_job(). The guards in .job_setup() refuse an unfinished render: an item
# that still reads a draft job, or a file still holding an EDIT: marker, is
# listed in a callout rather than passed off as a result.
.job <- hvtiRtemplates:::.job_setup(SUBJECT, TYPE, envir = environment())
.root <- .job$root
set_path <- .job$set_path
.provenance_data <- list()
# The draft banners, if any, and the box under the title, after all the code above.
.job$notice
```

## Question

```{r}
#| label: edit-question
#| results: asis
# EDIT: paste the research question from the protocol, word for word. The
# report is judged against this sentence, so do not paraphrase it.
QUESTION <- "Does the early hazard of death differ from the late hazard?"
cat("> ", QUESTION, "\n", sep = "")
```
